title: Calling genotypes

blocks.what_we_do: Read the call and score columns without treating the score as certainty.
blocks.why: The calling algorithm compares intensities with expected clusters. A GC score is a calling-quality measure; it is not a probability that an association is true, nor a p-value. A no-call can reflect low signal or ambiguous clusters. The examples use semicolons and decimal points intentionally: check the delimiter instead of changing the computer language.
blocks.command:
```{r s1-5}
lines <- readLines(reports[1], warn = FALSE)
start <- match("[Data]", lines)
example <- read.table(text = lines[(start + 1L):length(lines)], sep = ";", header = TRUE, quote = "", check.names = FALSE, colClasses = "character")
head(example)
summary(as.numeric(example[["GC Score"]]))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: no PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.
blocks.expected_result:
Columns SNP Name, Sample ID, GC Score, Allele1 - Plus and Allele2 - Plus. The examples are selected report excerpts, not the full 299,523-site matrix for every person.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows with the supplied simulated dataset.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Does GC Score = 0.9 mean a variant has a 90% chance of causing disease?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The score concerns genotype calling, not causal or association evidence.

</details>
